title: Dependency Orbit: cross-team hotspots, slack windows, and escalation registry
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Problem: As Redwood scales, roadmaps in different teams (Eng, Design, Security, Infra) create transient capacity hotspots and tight handoffs that cause repeated last-minute scope shifts. Existing dependency lists are scattered across docs and calendar invites; we need an operational registry that surfaces hotspots (high-risk, high-impact dependencies), suggested slack windows, and an automated escalation path for blocked handoffs.

Goal: Ship a lightweight "Dependency Orbit" registry and UI pattern in the Roadmap Signals project that: (1) identifies cross-team hotspots for upcoming cycles, (2) recommends soft buffer windows based on past drift metrics, (3) ties each dependency to an escalation contact and fallback policy, (4) exposes readiness signals to release owners and stakeholders.

Scope: MVP covers dependencies between PM, Eng, Design, Security, and Infra for Q2 initiatives with API surface for automated feeds (Engineering readiness pings, design reviews, security signoffs). UI will be a new tab in the Roadmap Signals dashboard plus a lightweight CSV import/export for offline planning.

Out of scope: Automated pull requests to repos, deep integrations with external calendars for MVP (we will provide links and suggested windows), and complex machine-learning predictions for lead times (future iteration).

Why this matters: Reduces late cut or slippage by surfacing where teams need to negotiate contingency lanes earlier. Enables program managers to re-allocate buffer or request additional capacity proactively.

Proposed implementation:
- Backend: new registry table for dependency records (key fields: owning team, dependent team, artifact link, criticality score, preferred slack window, escalation contact, fallback variant).
- Ingest: CSV uploader + webhook endpoint for periodic readiness pings (schema v1).
- UI: "Orbit" tab showing sorted list of hotspots, timeline view with recommended slack windows, and quick actions (assign escalation, mark mitigated, add fallback).
- Signals: compute criticality using combined metrics (customer impact, number of downstream routes, historical drift). Configurable thresholds for what becomes a "hotspot".

Monitoring & rollout: start with 3 pilot initiatives (runtime-1.20 perf, console-2026.03 rollout, private-deploy pilot). Collect feedback for two cycles before wider enablement.

Risks: inaccurate criticality scoring could create noise; escalation fatigue if contacts are not kept up to date; incorrect slack windows could be gamed. Mitigations are clear: make scoring transparent, require owner confirmation, and provide an easy contact update flow.
acceptance_criteria: Registry accepts CSV import with required schema and persists records
Orbit tab shows at least three pilot hotspots with computed criticality and suggested slack windows
Each dependency record has an escalation contact and an assigned fallback policy
Webhook ingestion ingests readiness pings and updates readiness state visible in UI
Pilot stakeholders (PM, Eng, Design, Security, Infra) have signed off on the escalation flow
success_metrics: Reduction in last-minute scope cuts for pilot initiatives by >= 30% vs previous cycle
Average time-to-resolution for blocked handoffs reduced by 40% in pilot
>80% of pilot dependency records have an assigned escalation contact
Registry adoption: at least 3 teams creating/editing >10 dependencies during pilot
